+title: 'M5 Sessions: new, list, resume with replay, close'
+---
+## What
+
+`plan.md` -> **M5**.
+
+- **`session/new`** -- required absolute `cwd`, optional `mcpServers`, optional `additionalDirectories`. Response is `sessionId`. The v1 `modes` field is gone from the response.
+- **`session/list`** -- part of the required baseline.
+- **`session/resume`** -- replaces v1's `session/load`. Required `sessionId` and absolute `cwd`, optional `mcpServers`, `additionalDirectories`, and **`replayFrom`**. Omit `replayFrom` for a plain reconnect; send `{"type": "start"}` to replay the whole conversation as ordinary session updates. Response is `{}` and **may** include initial session config state.
+- **`session/close`** -- the agent **MUST** cancel that session's ongoing work and free its resources. Verify whether `session/delete` also exists (M0 resolves this).
+- **`session/set_config_option`** + `config_option_update` replace v1 modes. Categories include `mode`, `model`, `model_config`, `thought_level`.
+
+**MCP server config** (v2 shape): required **`type`** discriminator; `stdio` takes `command` / optional `args` / optional `env`; `http` takes `url` / optional `headers`. **`"type": "sse"` is removed.** Both gated by `session.mcp.stdio` / `session.mcp.http`.
+
+Replay is the mechanism that makes a reconnecting client correct rather than stale, so it is load-bearing for `FoundationModelsACPClient`.
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] All four session methods implemented and round-tripping.
+- [ ] `cwd` required and absolute; rejected otherwise at decode time.
+- [ ] `mcpServers` accepted on both `new` and `resume`, with the `type` discriminator required and `sse` absent.
+- [ ] `replayFrom` omitted vs `{"type":"start"}` produce reconnect vs full replay.
+- [ ] `session/close` cancels ongoing work.
+- [ ] Config options replace modes; `config_option_update` reported.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] Replay from start reproduces the full update sequence in order.
+- [ ] Plain resume (no `replayFrom`) replays nothing.
+- [ ] A relative `cwd` fails decoding.
+- [ ] An `sse` MCP config is rejected or surfaces as unknown, per the schema.
+- [ ] `session/close` with work in flight cancels it and frees resources.
+- [ ] Config option set + update round-trip for each category.

+    The M1 seam is closed — this card's "blocked on the M1 seam" note is resolved and has been removed from `plan.md`.
+
+    - `ResumeSessionRequest.replayFrom` is now `ReplayFrom?`, a tagged union with a `start(ReplayFromStart)` case and an `unknown(String, JSONValue)` fallback that keeps the whole raw cursor object beside the tag it could not name. That matters here specifically: the schema tells receivers that do not understand a cursor to "preserve the raw payload ... and otherwise reject the request rather than guessing where to replay from", which is only possible if the payload survived decoding.
+    - Config options are typed end to end. On the listing side `SessionConfigOption` is a struct with a nested `Payload` enum (`select(SessionConfigSelect)` / `boolean(SessionConfigBoolean)` / `unknown(String, JSONValue)`), carrying `configId`, `name`, `description`, and `category`. On the setting side `SetSessionConfigOptionRequest` is a struct with a nested `Value` enum (`id(SessionConfigValueId)` / `boolean(Bool)` / `other(String, JSONValue)`).
+    - One thing still untyped inside that surface: `SessionConfigSelect.options` is `SessionConfigSelectOptions`, which stays a `JSONValue` placeholder. It is an *untagged* union — an ungrouped array of options or a grouped one, told apart by payload shape with no discriminator — so there is nothing to key a Swift enum on. Resolving it needs a different emission model, not the seam work M1 did. `SessionConfigSelectGroup` stays an orphan for the same reason.

+

+
+- **`session/load` -> `session/resume` with `replayFrom`.** Replay is new; there is no v1 equivalent to lean on.
+- **MCP server config shape changed** — `"type": "sse"` is removed. The deleted `McpServerWireTests` covered the v1 three-variant union; recreate it for the v2 two-variant one.
+
+`deleteSession` **survives**: M0 confirmed `session/delete` is stable in v2, distinct from `session/close`, and gated on `capabilities.session.delete`. It is in scope here.
+
+## What
+
+`plan.md` -> **M5**.
+
+- **`session/new`** -- required absolute `cwd`, optional `mcpServers`, optional `additionalDirectories`. Response is `sessionId`. The v1 `modes` field is gone from the response.
+- **`session/list`** -- part of the required baseline.
+- **`session/resume`** -- replaces v1's `session/load`. Required `sessionId` and absolute `cwd`, optional `mcpServers`, `additionalDirectories`, and **`replayFrom`**. Omit `replayFrom` for a plain reconnect; send `{"type": "start"}` to replay the whole conversation as ordinary session updates. Response is `{}` and **may** include initial session config state.
+- **`session/close`** -- the agent **MUST** cancel that session's ongoing work (*"treat it as if `session/cancel` was called"*) and then free the session's resources.
+- **`session/delete`** -- a **different** operation from `close`: it removes an existing session *from `session/list`*. Takes `sessionId`, returns `{}`. **Capability-gated on `capabilities.session.delete`** (`SessionDeleteCapabilities`; omitted or `null` both mean unsupported, `{}` means supported), so unlike the other four it is not part of the session baseline and must default to method-not-found when unadvertised.
+- **`session/set_config_option`** + `config_option_update` replace v1 modes. Categories include `mode`, `model`, `model_config`, `thought_level`.
+
+**MCP server config** (v2 shape): required **`type`** discriminator; `stdio` takes `command` / optional `args` / optional `env`; `http` takes `url` / optional `headers`. **`"type": "sse"` is removed.** Both gated by `session.mcp.stdio` / `session.mcp.http`.
+
+Replay is the mechanism that makes a reconnecting client correct rather than stale, so it is load-bearing for `FoundationModelsACPClient`.
+
+*Blocked on the M1 seam:* `ResumeSessionRequest.replayFrom` is `JSONValue?` until `ReplayFrom` resolves, and config options are untyped end to end — `SessionConfigOption` on the listing side, the whole `session/set_config_option` params object on the setting side.

+- [ ] `session/close` cancels ongoing work.
+- [ ] `session/delete` is gated on `capabilities.session.delete` and defaults to method-not-found when unadvertised.
